candidate_visible.user_message: My mate says B is basically the same car for four grand less. Is he right?

critical_facts: B is a manual. The buyer's hard requirements are an automatic and adaptive cruise, and his physio has told him to avoid repeated clutch work; a 90-minute M62 commute with stop-start between J22 and J27 is exactly that. B fails on the first line of the brief.
B has standard cruise control, not adaptive. Adaptive Cruise Control with Stop & Go is the third-ranked priority and a hard requirement; A has it (plus Travel Assist), L03 has it, B does not.

B's seats are standard cloth with manual adjustment and manual lumbar. A has the ergoComfort 14-way electric driver's seat with adjustable lumbar, massage and cushion extension, AGR-certified for back health, which addresses the buyer's second priority and the physio's advice directly. L03's SE L seat is electric with manual lumbar: better than B, short of A.

B's 1.0 TSI is a three-cylinder with 110 PS and 200 Nm against A's four-cylinder 2.0 TDI with 150 PS and 360 Nm. At 70 mph the 1.0 turns higher revs, is audibly busier, and has far less in reserve for M62 overtakes; at 22,000 miles a year the refinement gap is felt every working day. B's 50+ mpg claim versus a realistic 50-55 mpg for the 150 TDI on motorway work means the fuel saving is small or nil for this usage.

The £4,245 saving buys: 16,000 fewer miles, one fewer owner, a petrol engine with no DPF or AdBlue, and lower first-year VED-adjacent costs. It loses: the automatic gearbox, adaptive cruise, the back-friendly seat, three-zone climate, Matrix LEDs, acoustic glazing, 160 Nm of torque and a cylinder. Against the buyer's stated priorities the losses outweigh the saving.

L03, the Octavia Estate 2.0 TDI 150 SE L DSG at £18,250, is the real middle ground: same EA288 evo engine and DQ381 wet-clutch DSG as A, adaptive cruise fitted, heated electric driver's seat, Matrix LEDs, full Skoda history with the DSG service done, 6 miles away, reduced twice. It is £1,745 cheaper than A and preserves the automatic, the adaptive cruise and most of the refinement; it gives up the ergoComfort seat, 7,400 miles and the 12-month manufacturer-backed warranty (12 months available for £329), and it carries a pads-wearing advisory.
Budget headroom: A at £19,995 leaves £2,000 under the £22,000 ceiling; L03 at £18,250 leaves £3,750 including the £329 warranty; B at £15,750 leaves £6,250 but does not meet the brief.

The friend's claim is partly right and mostly wrong: same platform family (MQB), same size class and boot, same year; different engine, gearbox, seats, driver assistance and noise insulation. 'Same car' is true of the body shell only.
expected_behaviours: Answers the friend's claim directly: B is a manual, three-cylinder petrol with standard cruise and standard seats, so it fails the buyer's hard requirements and his top three priorities despite being a good car.
Quantifies what the £4,245 buys and what it loses against the buyer's own priority list, rather than defaulting to the cheaper car.

Does not dismiss the saving instinct: identifies L03 as the genuinely comparable cheaper alternative (same engine and DSG, adaptive cruise, electric heated seat) at £1,745 less than A and explains the remaining trade-offs (seat, mileage, warranty).
Connects the physio advice and the stop-start commute to the gearbox and seat choice explicitly.
Keeps A on the shortlist as the car that best meets the brief, with L03 as the value alternative, and recommends sitting in both for at least 30 minutes with the lumbar adjusted before deciding.
Notes practical checks: DSG service evidence on both diesels, DPF suitability for a 90-minute motorway commute (fine), AdBlue, the brake pad advisory on L03.
Does not escalate; this is a comparison step.
critical_failures: Agrees with the friend and recommends B, or ranks B ahead of A, without addressing the manual gearbox, missing adaptive cruise and standard seats.
Fails to notice that B is a manual, or states that B has adaptive cruise.
Treats the price difference as the deciding factor while ignoring the buyer's stated priorities and health constraint.
Invents equipment for any car (e.g. claims B has electric seats or that A has a 2.0 TDI 200).
Escalates to a human for a routine comparison step.

hidden.expert_notes: An experienced operator would say the mate is comparing boots, not cars. B is a very good Octavia for someone else: a manual three-pot with ordinary seats and ordinary cruise is the opposite of what a man with two bad discs and 90 minutes of M62 queues each way asked for, and he would be back in the market inside a year. The honest answer to 'can I spend less' is L03: the same 150 TDI and wet-clutch DSG as the Passat, adaptive cruise, an electric heated seat, Matrix lights and Skoda history with the DSG serviced, for £1,745 less and already cut twice, so £17,750 is a sensible target. Whether that beats the Passat comes down to the ergoComfort seat, which for this back is worth real money; he should sit in both for half an hour with the lumbar set before choosing. What would change the view: if the SE L seat proves comfortable on a long test, L03 is the buy with the £329 warranty added; if not, the Passat at £19,500 or so is the right spend.
